agree.reason: Opening with Dana's own $600K figure and closing with a clear break-even makes a 20-minute call easy to justify, though the email gives her nothing she could take to her IT director.

honest.reason: It ties the halving to one named customer instead of claiming 'we cut errors in half' across the board, and every number traces back to the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $75,000 annual cost for five sites and the roughly 13% break-even, but it never applies the pet-supply customer's 54% cut to her $600K, which would show about $320K in avoided returns.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is set out correctly as returns staying at about $600K a year, though the email doesn't say plainly that this cost repeats every year if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: Asking 'whether those numbers hold up for your operation' admits the result comes from one customer, but it names no measure Dana could check, no date and no consequence.

objections.reason: Saying 'it sits on top of' the WMS goes partway toward the IT director's resistance, but it doesn't say how little IT work is needed or that the current system stays untouched.

fit.reason: It is short, uses brief paragraphs that read well on a phone, has a pointed subject line and asks for one thing.
